trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Tag_Processor with documented constructor, next_tag('img'), add_class('wp-image'), and get_updated_html(). This is the correct flat class-attribute edit pattern, preserves untouched bytes, skips comments, matches tag names case-insensitively, and leaves incomplete trailing tags unmodified.

Same documented, idiomatic Tag Processor solution as the reference. No unsupported APIs and no _doing_it_wrong records. Correctly relies on add_class for existing class preservation and get_updated_html for byte-preserving output.

Same documented, idiomatic Tag Processor solution as trials 1 and 2. Correct processor choice, documented calls only, and appropriate handling of comments, case-insensitive tag matching, unquoted untouched attributes, and incomplete input through next_tag/get_updated_html behavior.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all 8 hidden cases, so there were no observed failed cases to diagnose. The rendered docs supported this task well: the Tag Processor overview explicitly says to use it for flat tag/class/attribute work and byte-precise edits; next_tag() documents string tag-name queries, ASCII case-insensitive matching, skipping tag-like text in comments/raw-text content, and pausing before incomplete trailing tokens; add_class() documents appending without removing or reordering existing classes; get_updated_html() documents returning queued edits while preserving untouched bytes. Near-miss: the exact placement of a newly created class attribute is inferable from the general attribute-update rules, but not stated directly in add_class().

doc_gaps.problem: It states that a missing class attribute is created, but does not explicitly say where that new attribute is inserted relative to existing attributes.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general contract sentence and example: when add_class creates a new class attribute, it follows the same new-attribute insertion rules as set_attribute, so the class attribute is inserted immediately after the tag name while unrelated existing attributes retain their original bytes.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor page lists inherited add_class(), but its local section is much thinner than the Tag Processor page and omits the append/no-duplicate/preservation details relevant to callers choosing between the two docs.
doc_gaps.suggestion: For inherited mutation methods, either inline the full inherited contract or add an explicit cross-reference summary covering class append semantics, duplicate handling, and get_updated_html as the retrieval method after mutations.
